# dsh-monitor
A monitoring plugin for DeepSeek Harness: machine health, runtime state, the git repositories you wo
rk in, and the Kubernetes cluster you develop on — from one sidebar entry, without leaving the app.
The **Système** entry carries four sub-views, switched from the tabs at the top of the panel: **Mach
ine** answers « is this machine healthy? » in one scroll, **Kubernetes** answers « what runs in the
cluster, what is degraded, and why? », **Dépôts** answers « what is the state of the git workspace,
and what is left to push? », and **Applications** answers « what is installed on this Mac, and what
is out of date? ». The four interfaces are written in French.
## What it shows
- **Machine** — CPU, memory, disk, load average, battery, swap, the top processes and a **Processeur
** card that draws the processor over time. A sample is appended to `cpu.jsonl` every 60 s, whether
the panel is open or not, and kept for 24 h; the card reads that file back in one of three windows (
1 h, 6 h, 24 h — it opens on 1 h), draws the average of each bucket as one curve, says for every poi
nt what the average and the peak were over its measures, sums the window up (current, minimum, avera
ge, maximum), and explains itself instead of showing a blank plot when the file holds nothing yet. M
emory follows the Activity Monitor definition (app + wired + compressed) instead of the naive `total
- free`, which sits at ~99 % as soon as the OS keeps inactive pages. CPU is a delta over a real tim
e window on both platforms: a `/proc/stat` sample on Linux, the second `top -l 2 -s 1` sample on mac
OS. Linux reads `/proc/meminfo`, `/proc/stat`, `/proc/swaps` and `/sys/class/power_supply` directly.
When Colima is present, its VM disk is measured through `colima ssh -- df -kP` and reported separat

ely from the host disk.
- **DSH** — active sessions, running jobs, startup errors over 24 h, cache s

ize, recent sessions, and today's cost when `costLedger` points to a JSON ledger.

## Configuration
The plugin is configured on its `cordis.patch.yml` entry, from a page the package brings to **Plugin
s → Système**. Saving the page writes the values into the profile patch (the YAML below), so the con
figuration stays in the profile's own file.
The page is split in four sections: **Général** first, with the panel refresh cadence, then **Dépôts
git**, **Kubernetes** and **Applications**. The Applications section is only shown on macOS; its fi
rst switch hides the tab, its second asks Homebrew (without it the bundle reading still runs). The c
ontext picker sits in the header of the Kubernetes view: it lists the contexts `kubectl` declares on
the machine, plus an automatic entry, the default, that follows the current context, and writes the
choice straight to `k8sContext`. The cluster check asks that context for its version and makes no a
ssumption about the cluster's flavour. Each of those last two opens with a switch that hides the mat
ching tab — the switch only changes what the panel shows, the collection keeps running in the backgr
ound so the view comes back with its current values when switched on again.
| Key | Default | Meaning |

| `projectsRoot` | `~/projects` | Directory holding the git repositories to watch |
| `showRepos` |

`true` | Show the Dépôts tab |
| `k8sContext` | `''` | Watched `kubectl` context, chosen from the Ku
bernetes card of the panel among the contexts the machine detects; empty follows the current context

|
| `showK8s` | `true` | Show the Kubernetes sections |
| `showApps` | `true` | Show the Applicatio

ns tab (macOS only) |
| `showBrew` | `true` | Ask Homebrew when the Applications tab is read — `brew

--version`, `brew list`, `brew outdated`; off limits the tab to the bundles |
| `costLedger` | `~/.
dsh/storages/cost-meter/ledger.json` | Ledger written by `dsh-cost-meter` (`days.<YYYY-MM-DD>.cost`,
`.calls`, `config.currency`/`config.symbol`); empty hides the cost row. Not shown on the page — ove

rride it in the YAML only when the ledger lives elsewhere |
| `refreshSeconds` | `60` | Panel refres
h cadence, in seconds, clamped between `15` and `900` |

## Prerequisites
- DeepSeek Harness `>=0.2.1-rc.5 <0.3.0-0`. The range sits in `engines.dsh`, so a host outside it re

fuses the plugin rather than loading a panel it was never tested against.
- The app's own Node runti

me, 20 or later. Nothing else is installed for the panel to work.
- macOS or Linux. Windows is not s

upported: the machine collectors branch on `process.platform` and otherwise read procfs.
- Optional
tools. Each one enables a part of the panel; without it that part is hidden or reads `—`, never an e
. Each one enables a part of the panel; without it that part is hidden or reads `—`, never an error:
| Tool | Without it |

| `gh`, authenticated | pull request columns show `—` |
| `kubectl`, plus `docker` or `colima`, plus

`kind` | the `Kubernetes` tab is hidden |
| `git`, with checkouts under `projectsRoot` | the `Dépôt

ernetes` tab is hidden |
| `git`, with checkouts under `projectsRoot` | the `Dépôts` tab is hidden |
- No configuration file is required: the defaults (`~/projects`, a 60 s refresh, local same-origin r
equests only) apply as is.
## Architecture
- `lib/index.js` — server side: collectors, thresholds, actions, journal. Routes `/systeme/api/etat`
, `/systeme/api/disque`, `/systeme/api/action`, `/systeme/api/journal`, `/systeme/api/reglages`, `/s
ysteme/api/app`, `/systeme/api/app/footprint`, `/systeme/api/cpu`. Requests must be local and same-o

rigin; anything else gets a 403.
- `lib/apps.js` — the macOS reading: the app folders scanned, each
bundle's `Info.plist` and signature, the Homebrew formulae and casks, and the join that says whether
a cask and its bundle agree. Bounded by one `brew` call batch and a per-bundle `plutil`, and skippe

d entirely when Homebrew is switched off.
- `lib/k8s.js` — the Kubernetes reading: raw `kubectl` obj
ects in, one model out (counters, capacity, causes, namespace rows, topology, components, activity).

Pure and unit-tested, so the panel logic is verified without a live cluster.
- `lib/client.js` — th
e React panel loaded by the DSH client — `Système`, with its `Machine`, `Kubernetes`, `Dépôts` and `

Applications` views — styles scoped under `.dsh-systeme` and `.dsh-kube`.
- `cordis.patch.yml` — ins
erts the `systeme` entry.
